result.evidence: I could message about an actual delay, not report every movement.
result.answer:
Agreed: you commit to sending a message when an already-agreed plan is delayed; Ning commits to handling ordinary quiet times on his own (text once, tell himself 'busy, not gone'), and you both agreed that if his anxiety resurfaces he names it once and you may reply 'limit stands' without it becoming a fight. He also accepted the refusal of continuous tracking.

Proposals, not agreed: Ning's suggestion of a 'heads up, I'll be offline for a bit' message before you go quiet — you responded with a question, never accepted or declined it. Trip-specific location sharing: you said you 'could discuss' it, asked about limits, then explicitly stated you had changed your mind and would not do it, and Ning accepted ('no trip sharing, that's your call').

Not yet done: no delay message has actually been sent in this practice, so the delay-message arrangement exists only as words — it is an agreed commitment awaiting its first real use. No offline heads-up was decided either way, so nothing remains pending except putting the agreed delay-message plan into practice.
